newsitem.title: GERMANY: Grundig wants to break even in 98 - report.
newsitem.headline: Grundig wants to break even in 98 - report.

text.p: Troubled German electronics group Grundig will seek to break even in 1998, a year earlier than planned, the group's top executive told a German magazine in an interview on Sunday.

Grundig management board chairman Pieter de Jong told the magazine Focus that he believed the group, which was abandoned this year by its backer Philips N.V. due to massive losses, would not survive if it posted losses over the next two years.
He also said the trust of creditor banks has been strained and said Grundig must go forward with its plan to slash 1,700 jobs and focus on television production.
"Our goal is to save 350 million marks in the next two years," de Jong told the magazine, noting the combining of three plants in the Nuremberg area would save about 20 million marks a year.

Grundig lost 553 million marks in 1996 on sales of 3.3 billion marks, prompting Dutch-based Philips to pull its support in April for Grundig because the losses have weighed heavily on Philips' earnings.

De Jong said the first two months of 1997 were a "catastrophe" but that sales began to rebound in April and reaffirmed the group's goal to be the top television seller in Europe by 2005 with sales of about five billion marks.
Grundig intends to focus on winning more market share in the television market, pinning its hopes on a new "super flat" television screen to come into the market next year.
He reaffirmed that Philips was committed to working with Grundig, saying Philips had invested about two billion marks into Grundig and would keep up the alliance in the future.
